sections.h2: Where to record a Butler County deed
sections.html:
Butler County runs one recorder's office, at 130 High Street, Hamilton, OH 45011. The front desk answers at 513-887-3192, email goes to recorder@bcohio.gov, and conveyance or transfer questions go to 513-887-3154.

Sellers from Middletown, Fairfield, Oxford, Monroe, Trenton and Sharonville all file in that same building. The office promises 24 hour turnaround if you include a self addressed stamped return envelope. Its website offers a record search going back to 1987. Because recorded papers are generally public, strangers can read whatever is on your deed, so skip any personal detail the form does not call for.

The current schedule took effect January 1, 2025. A deed, mortgage or lease of two pages or fewer is $39.00, which includes the $5.00 preservation surcharge, and $8.00 more is charged for each further page. Section 317.32 explains the total: $17, plus $17 for the housing trust fund, on the first two pages, and up to $5 more at the county's option. Schedules get revised, so request the latest copy before you write a check.

Recorder's fees effective January 1, 2025
Document or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage, lease, up to two pages$39.00, surcharge included

Satisfaction, release, assignment or amendment$4.00 per reference
Copy of recorded document$2.00 per page
Certification$1.00 per document
Transfer and conveyance fee$3.00 per $1,000.00 of purchase price
Parcel fee with a deed50 cents per parcel number

A deed that skipped the auditor gets turned away at the recorder. The buyer files a statement of value under section 319.202, and the auditor then notes the fee on the deed. Take a conveyance or exemption form and all parcel numbers with you.

Two laws sit behind the one rate printed on the schedule:

  • A state-set auditor fee, section 319.54(G)(3), for handling the value statement: one dollar minimum, or ten cents per $100 or part of $100.
  • An optional county charge, section 322.02, capped at thirty cents per $100, which the grantor pays the auditor.
  • What the schedule actually says: $3.00 per $1,000 of price, check to the Butler County Auditor, and 50 cents for each parcel number on the deed.

With several parcels on one deed the parcel charge multiplies, so phone 513-887-3154 before you file.

Some deeds escape the auditor's fee under section 319.54(G)(3), but you still must state the exemption reason on the filing. Family and estate sales often involve:

  • Gifts between spouses, or from a parent to a child.
  • Corrective deeds that repair a mistake in an earlier deed.
  • Deeds that only secure or release a debt.
  • Court-ordered transfers, though not a sale carried out under the order.
  • Transfers where nothing at all is paid and no gift is involved.
  • A grantee who is not a dealer and takes title only to resell soon after.

The statute lists many more, from government transfers to deeds worth $100 or less. Check with the auditor on which exemption form belongs with the deed.

Section 317.114 covers papers prepared after June 30, 2009, and a document that violates the layout rules costs an extra $20.00. Court papers, plats, DD214s and state or federal documents do not have to follow them. The standards are:

  • Paper from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches, with text of at least 10 point.
  • Black or blue ink only, and no highlighter.
  • A one inch margin on both sides and at the bottom.
  • Page one keeps its top three inches empty for the recorder, auditor and engineer stamps.
  • Later pages need a one and a half inch top margin.

Content rules apply too. Every document needs a legal description, affidavits must name the current owner, and papers notarized in Ohio need a prepared by statement. Blanket assignments and blanket satisfactions are refused, so a lender that paid off several loans must prepare a separate release for each.

You can skip the counter. Simplifile, CSC and the eRecording Partners Network all deliver deeds electronically, whichever the closing office prefers. The county's free Property Alert will email you when a paper is recorded under a name or legal description you sign up with. Landlords, owners of empty houses and heirs can catch a fraudulent filing that way.

Two fee notices are posted on the home page: the 2025 increases and an older 2022 notice on the reference fee. Packets printed before those dates may carry outdated amounts.

sections.h2: Recording a sale step by step
sections.html: The title agent or an attorney drafts the deed, using the full legal description and parcel number. You sign in front of a notary. Someone checks the deed against the layout rules above. It goes to the auditor with the conveyance form and a check for the transfer fee, then on to the recorder for the page fee and recording. The original returns in your envelope, or the closing office gets a confirmation for an electronic filing. If you cannot make it to the counter, the title company can do all of this for you.

sections.h2: The county and the local market
sections.html: Butler County, in southwestern Ohio, had 390,357 people in 2020 and an estimate of 400,128 for 2025, with Hamilton as seat and largest city. About 69.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median value is $258,500 and median household income is $81,590. Most of the county lies in the Great Miami and Little Miami river valleys. The 1913 flood hit Hamilton and Middletown hard, with 46 percent of Hamilton under water, so ask about flood history when a house sits near the Great Miami.

Selling for cash changes nothing about the route: deed, then auditor, then recorder, usually carried by the closing agent. A seller who drafts the deed personally should phone the auditor about the transfer charge and the recorder about page count before signing. Skipping a mortgage lender means no lender-driven delays, but the county steps stay. Ask the closing agent early which exemption form, if any, applies, and confirm the fee amounts the same week you close.

For an inherited house, the signer needs authority from the estate, and the title agent can say which probate documents must be attached. A seller with an old mortgage should confirm that the lender recorded its release, because an unreleased lien blocks clean title. Bring photo ID, the parcel number and any payoff letters to the closing so nothing stalls at the counter.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Butler County recorder?
faqs.a: The main desk is 513-887-3192, or write recorder@bcohio.gov. For transfer and conveyance questions use 513-887-3154. Visit 130 High Street in Hamilton.

faqs.q: What does a two-page deed cost in Butler County?
faqs.a: $39.00 under the schedule effective January 1, 2025, with the $5.00 preservation surcharge built in. Extra pages are $8.00 each. Ask the office for its newest sheet before filing.

faqs.q: Whose name goes on the Butler County transfer fee check?
faqs.a: The Butler County Auditor. The rate is $3.00 per $1,000 of purchase price, with 50 cents more per parcel number on a deed.

faqs.q: Can a Butler County deed be filed electronically?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile, CSC or the eRecording Partners Network. Your closing office picks whichever it already uses.

faqs.q: Will Butler County accept a deed with no legal description?
faqs.a: No. A legal description is required on every document, and deeds also need parcel identification numbers, or the filing is refused.
